title: Finite affine chart families with fixed presentations along an affine inverse limit
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set, $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$, quasi-compact quasi-separated $S_{i_0}$-schemes $X_0,Y_0$, and a morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ over $S_{i_0}$ which is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For $i\geq i_0$ define $X_i,Y_i,f_i$ by base change to $S_i$, and define $X,Y,f$ by base change to $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There exist a finite affine open cover $Y_0=\bigcup_aV_{a,0}$, affine opens $W_{a,0}\subseteq S_{i_0}$ containing the image of $V_{a,0}$, and finite affine open covers $f_0^{-1}(V_{a,0})=\bigcup_bU_{ab,0}$, with the following properties.
For each $a$ write $W_{a,0}=\operatorname{Spec}R_{a,0}$, and let $W_{a,i}$ and $W_a$ be its inverse images in $S_i$ and $S$. These opens are affine; their coordinate rings $R_{a,i}$ form a directed system with the restriction-induced transition maps, and $W_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$ for $R_a=\varinjlim_{i\geq i_0}R_{a,i}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. There are fixed commutative $R_{a,0}$-algebras $B_{a,0},C_{ab,0}$ and $R_{a,0}$-algebra maps $\varphi_{ab,0}:B_{a,0}\to C_{ab,0}$ of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $B_{a,i}=R_{a,i}\otimes_{R_{a,0}}B_{a,0}$ and $C_{ab,i}=R_{a,i}\otimes_{R_{a,0}}C_{ab,0}$. The inverse-image opens $V_{a,i},U_{ab,i}$ identify with $\operatorname{Spec}B_{a,i},\operatorname{Spec}C_{ab,i}$ and their restricted morphism identifies with $\operatorname{Spec}(1\otimes\varphi_{ab,0})$. The same assertion holds at the limit, replacing $R_{a,i}$ by $R_a$. Each arrow identification consists of source and target isomorphisms making the morphism square commute. For every $i\geq i_0$, $Y_i=\bigcup_aV_{a,i}$ and $f_i^{-1}(V_{a,i})=\bigcup_bU_{ab,i}$; the corresponding opens also cover at the limit. Empty source covers are allowed. No finite presentation of $B_{a,0}$ over $R_{a,0}$ is assumed or asserted.

proof.text: Write $y_0:Y_0\to S_{i_0}$ for the structure map. For each point $y\in Y_0$, choose an affine open $W_y\subseteq S_{i_0}$ containing $y_0(y)$, and then an affine open $V_y$ containing $y$ inside the open $y_0^{-1}(W_y)$, using the affine-open basis twice. These $V_y$ cover $Y_0$. Quasi-compactness of $Y_0$ selects finitely many of them; label them $V_{a,0}$ and retain their associated $W_{a,0}$. This proves the required target/base incidence without requiring $Y_0\to S_{i_0}$ to be of finite presentation. If $Y_0$ is empty, take the empty family.

source.place: Tag 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic), first proof paragraph; Schemes Tag 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens)

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of qcqs morphism permanence to $f_0$: its source $X_0$ is quasi-compact and its target $Y_0$ is quasi-separated, so $f_0$ is quasi-compact. Each $V_{a,0}$ is quasi-compact because it is affine. The quasi-compact-inverse-image lemma therefore makes $f_0^{-1}(V_{a,0})$ quasi-compact. Apply the finite-affine-cover lemma to this open subscheme to choose $U_{ab,0}$, with finitely many $b$ for each $a$. An affine open of an open subscheme is an affine open of $X_0$. An empty inverse image can have no source charts.

source.place: Tag 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic), first proof paragraph; Schemes Tags 03GI (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence), 01K4 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine)

proof.text: Fix the canonical affine identifications with coordinate rings $R_{a,0}=\Gamma(W_{a,0},\mathcal O)$, $B_{a,0}=\Gamma(V_{a,0},\mathcal O)$, and $C_{ab,0}=\Gamma(U_{ab,0},\mathcal O)$. The restricted structure maps give their $R_{a,0}$-algebra structures. The restricted $f_0$ induces $\varphi_{ab,0}:B_{a,0}\to C_{ab,0}$; it respects $R_{a,0}$ because $f_0$ is over $S_{i_0}$. The affine-opens finite-presentation lemma applied to the locally finitely presented $f_0$ says precisely that each $\varphi_{ab,0}$ is finitely presented. The spectrum functor identifies the restricted morphisms with the spectrum maps of these ring maps. One $B_{a,0}$ is fixed for all $b$, including when there are no $b$; no finite presentation over $R_{a,0}$ is used.

source.place: Tag 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), (1) implies (2); Schemes affine-open convention following Definition 01IJ

proof.text: For $i\geq i_0$, affineness of $S_i\to S_{i_0}$ makes $W_{a,i}$ affine by definition. The affine-transition limit lemma makes $S\to S_{i_0}$ affine and identifies $W_a$ as the inverse limit of the $W_{a,i}$. Define $R_{a,i}=\Gamma(W_{a,i},\mathcal O)$. For $j\geq i\geq i_0$, restricting $S_j\to S_i$ gives $W_{a,j}\to W_{a,i}$, hence $R_{a,i}\to R_{a,j}$; functoriality of pullback on sections gives identities and composition. The tail $i\geq i_0$ is nonempty and directed: it contains $i_0$ and an upper bound of two of its elements still lies in the tail. The affine case of the same limit lemma therefore gives $W_a\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_a$, where $R_a=\varinjlim_{i\geq i_0}R_{a,i}$, with the indicated projections induced by the colimit maps. Use the coordinate-ring affine identifications throughout.

Let $T\to S_{i_0}$ be either $S_i\to S_{i_0}$ or $S\to S_{i_0}$, and write $A=R_{a,i}$ or $R_a$. Apply the affine-chart base-change isomorphism to $Z=Y_0$, $V=V_{a,0}$, $W=W_{a,0}$ and the fixed $R_{a,0}$-algebra $B_{a,0}$. It gives the inverse-image target open as $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{R_{a,0}}B_{a,0})$, with both projections specified. Apply it again to $Z=X_0$, $V=U_{ab,0}$ and $C_{ab,0}$ to obtain the source isomorphism. Under these isomorphisms the candidate $\operatorname{Spec}(1\otimes\varphi_{ab,0})$ has the required composites to $V_{a,0}$ and to the inverse image of $W_{a,0}$: on rings it sends $1\otimes b$ to $1\otimes\varphi_{ab,0}(b)$ and $a\otimes1$ to $a\otimes1$. The actual restriction of $f_T$ has the same two composites by the base-change square. The target open is their fibre product, so its universal property makes these arrows equal. Thus the chosen source and target isomorphisms give the commuting morphism square for every stage and for the limit, using the same $B_{a,0},C_{ab,0},\varphi_{ab,0}$.

Let $p_Y:Y_T\to Y_0$ and $p_X:X_T\to X_0$ denote the projections. Inverse images commute with unions, so $Y_T=p_Y^{-1}(\bigcup_aV_{a,0})=\bigcup_aV_{a,T}$. Since $p_Y\circ f_T=f_0\circ p_X$, one has $f_T^{-1}(V_{a,T})=p_X^{-1}(f_0^{-1}(V_{a,0}))=\bigcup_b p_X^{-1}(U_{ab,0})=\bigcup_bU_{ab,T}$. This proves both cover assertions for $T=S_i$ and $T=S$. If an original inverse image is empty, its pullback is empty and the same union equality holds for the empty source family.

Tag-label pairs 01YW/01YX/01TQ confirmed in tags/tags. Each step uses what its cited statements actually say. S1: affine-opens basis applied twice, then a finite subcover from quasi-compactness. S2: qcqs permanence (1) gives f_0 quasi-compact (X_0 qc, Y_0 qs), so the preimage of an affine is qc and has a finite affine cover; no affine intersections are assumed. S3: canonical Γ-identifications; lfp-affine-opens gives φ finitely presented; one B_{a,0} serves every b. S4: affine transitions make W_{a,i} affine; the limit-affine-transition open clause plus its affine clause on the directed tail give R_a = colim R_{a,i}. S5: affine-chart-base-change-iso (Lean-closed) applied to both source and target, hypotheses verified; the arrow square follows from projection composites and the fibre-product universal property. S6: elementary union and inverse-image computation. Edge cases tested: empty covers, zero rings, constant system, non-separated Y_0, and B not finite type over R. No duplicate of the item in the DAG (nagata morphism-descent and qc-open-chart nodes differ).
